requirements.text: Status: implementation design, 2026-10-24. This document proposes changes; it does not report an implementation, a deployment, or a change to the archive.

Inputs: Term Cards and Term Links proposal and zt-check gate proposal. The implementation baseline inspected for this design is commit `bab6bd7`. The proposals remain the feature specification; this document resolves how to build the features together.
Navigation: Architecture · Design decisions · Shared checker · Policy and ratchet · Term storage · Term-card compiler · Deterministic linking · Workflows · Verification · Feature coverage.

requirements.heading: The design in one page
requirements.text: Keep the three existing executables, the existing archive, and the existing digest ledger. Turn the existing `zt-check` crate into a pure checking library with an optional command-line adapter. Link that library into `zt`. Teach the existing Link machinery the Term-link syntax. Add one term-name column to Cards, one derived term-structure module, and two digest commands.

requirements.heading: The design in one page
requirements.text: A Term list, a Term Card, and a Term part all have type `term`. Their role comes from their term name and Location. They are Cards in the current archive, with the current Access, Lock, move, revision, receipt, and dump behavior. Their explanation is authored Markdown, rather than a second definition store.

requirements.heading: The design in one page
requirements.text: The service checks a proposed Card against the same rule implementation that `zt-check` uses. The service owns the final decision because it has current transaction context. The standalone tool predicts that decision when it has matching rules, policy, limits, metadata, and context. An incomplete offline check must say that it is incomplete.

requirements.heading: The design in one page
requirements.text: The new digest work consists of:

requirements.heading: The design in one page
requirements.text: `zt-digest term-cards`: plan source-bound jobs, accept DeepSeek JSON, check and review it, render Cards, then publish in table order through existing receipts.

requirements.heading: The design in one page
requirements.text: `zt-digest term-link`: compute byte-range substitutions in one book, show a plan, then apply guarded edits. No model chooses or writes a substitution.

requirements.heading: The design in one page
requirements.text: Do not create a terminology database, a gate process, a plugin framework, a new queue, a term-ownership table, or an independent Link parser for the digest.

requirements.heading: Minimal new structure
requirements.text: `the shared rule core` — The existing rules, structured diagnostics, and Card checks without I/O — The service must use the actual checker without spawning itself

requirements.heading: Minimal new structure
requirements.text: `shared text operations` — Shared envelope and lexical Link parsing, visible-text projection, and term-table parsing — Labels, scopes, rendering, and checks must agree on the text and target of a Term link

requirements.heading: Minimal new structure
requirements.text: `shared rule policy` — Rule catalog, defaults, overrides, severity, and legacy-fault comparison — The gate and self-check must make the same decision

requirements.heading: Minimal new structure
requirements.text: `the service gate adapter` — Load bounded transaction context and call the pure checker — Storage reads and write results belong in `zt`

requirements.heading: Minimal new structure
requirements.text: `the term-structure module` — Compute list/head/part roles and the term structure from Cards — Readers and write validation need one definition of a Term Card

requirements.heading: Minimal new structure
requirements.text: `the Term-card compiler` — The Term-card compiler — Generated explanations need checking, review, publication, and recovery

requirements.heading: Minimal new structure
requirements.text: `the Term-link command` — The deterministic link pass — Linking needs a reusable plan/apply operation

requirements.heading: Minimal new structure
requirements.text: Two workflow modules — Wire these commands into the existing compiler and relay paths — The two new stages have different execution contracts

requirements.heading: Minimal new structure
requirements.text: Two prompt files — Writer instructions and independent mathematical review — Content creation and review need separate tasks

requirements.heading: Minimal new structure
requirements.text: `core.rs`, `text.rs`, and `policy.rs` are files inside the existing checker crate, not new crates. Preserve `check.rs` as the CLI/input compatibility adapter. Do not split the rule implementation into one module per rule family merely to mirror the proposal diagram. Extract a further module only when a concrete responsibility becomes hard to navigate.

requirements.heading: Minimal new structure
requirements.text: Production storage changes are one nullable `cards.term_name` column and the widened Card-type constraint. Use existing `metadata` rows for archive policy and existing `links.kind` for `term` occurrences. No new persistent table is required.

requirements.heading: Data flow
requirements.text: Architecture/stage flow contract: ; inputs["GUI, Session, shell, MCP, apply_batch"] --> tx["Existing write transaction"]; tx --> gate["gate.rs: proposed Card + bounded context"]; gate --> check["zt-check core + policy + text"]; check --> decision["Accept with warnings, or card_check"]; cli["zt-check CLI: drafts or archive reads"] --> check; drafts["DeepSeek JSON + independent math review"] --> compiler["zt-digest term-cards"]; compiler --> inputs; planner["zt-digest term-link: deterministic plan"] --> inputs; tx --> archive[("Existing SQLite archive")]; archive --> readers["Existing Card, GUI, Session, dump, and MCP readers"]

requirements.heading: What the current code actually provides

requirements.heading: Corrections to promises that the current structure cannot keep
requirements.text: **Bounded publication instead of one unbounded transaction.** Both new commands use existing receipt-backed chunks. A chunk is atomic; an entire large book is recoverable but not atomic. Reports distinguish planned, committed, pending, and refused items. This preserves the current batch contract.

requirements.heading: Corrections to promises that the current structure cannot keep
requirements.text: **Checked publication prefixes instead of arbitrary holes.** The proposal permits successful drafts to publish while others fail, and also demands table-row placement order. Publish the longest contiguous prefix of ready terms, never a later row ahead of an unresolved earlier row. Keep later ready drafts on disk. This supports partial progress without address reservations, placeholders, or moving already published Cards. Section 12 specifies recovery.

requirements.heading: Corrections to promises that the current structure cannot keep
requirements.text: **Conditional prediction instead of unconditional offline acceptance.** An offline check without the archive's policy or required context cannot guarantee acceptance. It returns an incomplete result; the service preview is the authoritative preflight.

requirements.heading: Corrections to promises that the current structure cannot keep
requirements.text: **Stable faults instead of printed-line identity.** Use structured, unclipped diagnostic identity and multiplicity for the legacy ratchet. Printed lines remain the human-readable interface.

requirements.heading: Corrections to promises that the current structure cannot keep
requirements.text: **One shared lexical implementation.** Move reusable text/Link scanning into the existing checker crate's pure text module. `the root Link facade/lifecycle` remains the service-facing Link facade and lifecycle implementation, including address-grammar and storage checks. This avoids a dependency cycle and avoids three inconsistent regex implementations.

requirements.heading: Corrections to promises that the current structure cannot keep
requirements.text: **A persisted auto-link choice.** `link:false` must survive loss of the staging directory. Store it as an authored head line on the Term Card, rather than adding another column or relying on the draft file forever.

requirements.heading: Corrections to promises that the current structure cannot keep
requirements.text: **Self-checks precede enforcement.** Ship the compatible CLI, preview support, writer instructions, and `card_check` recovery before turning new agent blocking defaults on. The proposal's rollout list placed some of these after enforcement; that ordering would strand existing writers.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: These invariants define successful implementation.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: A Card's authored Markdown is the source of truth for its explanation and Link occurrences.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: A field or table computed from Cards is a projection, never an independent authority.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: Every authoring route checks the final proposed text and metadata inside the write transaction.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: Checking uses the proposed Workspace, type, facet, level, form, and term name, not the row's previous type.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: An agent can change only agent Cards. Gate policy cannot grant Access or unlock anything.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: A Lock refusal stops the affected operation without retries through another route.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: Existing envelope, field, Link, Access, and Lock invariants remain mandatory.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: A Term link reaches a term head directly; it does not resolve a name through a registry.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: A Term use contributes no reasoning edge, Model membership, or Idea inbound/outbound credit.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: Removing recognized Term-link markup preserves exactly the visible authored body bytes.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: A rerun with unchanged inputs makes no authored edits or new Card allocations.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: Preview changes no persisted Card, receipt, revision, allocation, or Lock history.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: A refusal rolls back the actual atomic operation, including receipts and allocations.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: Unknown context, a stale contract, or an interrupted check cannot be reported as a pass.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: Mathematical format checks and model review are evidence of review, not proof of mathematical truth.

requirements.heading: Invariants
requirements.text: A run with missing terms or unresolved refusals remains visibly incomplete even when the audit and report run successfully.

requirements.heading: Concrete inputs, not an extensibility framework
requirements.text: Use the existing JSON Card entry shape where it already serves the rules. Introduce only the small typed boundary needed to distinguish checking a proposed write from auditing stored Cards.

requirements.heading: Concrete inputs, not an extensibility framework
requirements.text: Conceptually:

requirements.heading: Concrete inputs, not an extensibility framework
requirements.text: Typed check contract: CheckInput carries card, before, context, policy and purpose; purpose distinguishes Write/Audit; CheckReport carries completeness, ordered diagnostics and blocker count; reuse existing Card entries rather than duplicate DTO families.

requirements.heading: Concrete inputs, not an extensibility framework
requirements.text: `CardEntry` includes the parsed envelope, address/kind/Workspace, type fields, and term-role facts. `before` is absent on a new Card. The actual Rust types should reuse the checker's existing entry representation; do not duplicate every field into several DTO families.

requirements.heading: Concrete inputs, not an extensibility framework
requirements.text: `CheckContext` is an immutable value containing the small set of facts needed for the selected rules:

requirements.heading: Concrete inputs, not an extensibility framework
requirements.text: Parent and relevant ancestors, with the old and proposed versions where required.

requirements.heading: Concrete inputs, not an extensibility framework
requirements.text: Referenced target identities and types.

requirements.text: Book/root identity and applicable Book term table.

requirements.text: Formal model setting/level/facet/shared membership facts for the checked Card.

requirements.text: The availability/completeness of each context family.

requirements.heading: Concrete inputs, not an extensibility framework
requirements.text: The service materializes this value using its transaction connection. The CLI materializes the same value from bundled entries or existing MCP reads. The core itself makes no I/O calls. A value seam is simpler than a trait whose methods hide database or MCP work.

requirements.heading: Concrete inputs, not an extensibility framework
requirements.text: Distinguish `absent` from `unavailable`. For example, an Idea Card may legitimately have unknown source evidence and receive I7 advice. A failed attempt to read its source context is an incomplete check, not the same semantic finding.

requirements.heading: Bounded context loading
requirements.text: For a write, load the proposed Card, required ancestry/setting, applicable term list, and distinct referenced targets. Reuse those facts within one batch transaction. Do not build `Snapshot::read` for the whole archive for every Card.

requirements.heading: Bounded context loading
requirements.text: Limits must be explicit and shared in the check contract. Start with existing batch and authored-input bounds. Bound context by the affected book/model and distinct requested targets; if a pathological model exceeds the supported check budget, return an incomplete/context-budget error rather than silently truncating or running an archive-wide scan.

requirements.heading: Bounded context loading
requirements.text: Graph rules remain an explicit audit path. Large context is not permission to quietly run I6 against every title at write time.

requirements.heading: One diagnostic representation
requirements.text: A diagnostic needs at least:

requirements.heading: One diagnostic representation
requirements.text: Structured public contract includes these fields and their stated example semantics: address, rule, fault, key, message, severity, legacy, scope.

requirements.heading: One diagnostic representation
requirements.text: Keep rule ids and current message wording unless a rule's semantics changes. Format the familiar line at the boundary:

requirements.heading: One diagnostic representation
requirements.text: K/14 E2 missing labels: 参与者、来源 K/14 R20 (advisory) ... faults: 1

requirements.heading: One diagnostic representation
requirements.text: Formatting collapses whitespace and clips as today. Identity does not. A fault's `key` is a rule-specific semantic key built from the full offending fragment or missing requirement, rather than a source line number or the clipped display string.

requirements.heading: One diagnostic representation
requirements.text: Preserve the current rule traversal order in the first extraction. Gate and CLI reports use the same ordering. Aggregate batch reports order by item, then the core's rule order, then occurrence.

requirements.heading: Policy ownership
requirements.text: The checker owns the rule catalog and default policy. The service owns the selected archive's effective overrides.

requirements.heading: Policy ownership
requirements.text: Use `metadata` keys such as `gate.agent.R2` and `gate.human.E2`. Extend `zt config set` for the declared `gate.<workspace>.<rule>` keys, routing the change to the selected archive under its normal writer lock. Do not put per-archive overrides in a process-global feature file or introduce a second config database.

requirements.heading: Policy ownership
requirements.text: Provide `zt config` output that names effective overrides and their archive. Missing override means the default, and an explicit reset removes the metadata row.

requirements.heading: Policy ownership
requirements.text: Validate rule ids, Workspace names, and values. Reject typos, unsupported rules, and attempts to override hard invariants. A graph-only rule cannot be configured to block a single write; refuse that override with a clear explanation.

requirements.heading: Policy ownership
requirements.text: A policy change receives a new policy hash and advances the revision used by check-contract readers. It does not rewrite Cards or persist old-fault baselines. Load the effective policy once per operation/transaction so an entire atomic batch uses one policy.

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm
requirements.text: New Cards have no legacy allowance. All configured blocking diagnostics can block them.

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm
requirements.text: For an existing Card:

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm
requirements.text: Check the old authored version using its old metadata and the same current rule version/policy snapshot.

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm
requirements.text: Check the final proposed version using proposed metadata and transaction context.

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm
requirements.text: For comparable rules, build a multiset keyed by `(rule, fault, key)` from the old report.

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm
requirements.text: Consume one old occurrence for each matching new occurrence.

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm
requirements.text: A matched diagnostic becomes `legacy:true` advice. An unmatched diagnostic keeps its configured severity.

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm
requirements.text: Refuse only if an unmatched blocking diagnostic remains.

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm
requirements.text: Do not compare clipped lines or merely sets. Adding a second copy of an already faulty sentence is a new occurrence. Moving an unchanged faulty paragraph to another line is not.

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm
requirements.text: A size fault's key includes its measured value and limit, so making an oversized Card larger is not grandfathered as the same fault. A missing-label fault includes the missing-label set. A fragment fault includes the unclipped offending fragment.

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm
requirements.text: On a type/role/level change, compare only rules whose applicability and meaning remain the same. A Card retyped from Idea to Event must satisfy newly applicable E-format rules. Do not run Event rules on the old Idea body and then call those newly relevant faults legacy. Use an explicit applicability signature, including model concept/formal transitions and term list/head/part transitions.

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm
requirements.text: The ratchet covers new quality rules, not hard storage invariants. It cannot legalize malformed Link syntax, invalid type fields, an unauthorized write, or a Lock violation. Retaining a previously broken target follows the existing Link grandfathering behavior, separately.

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm

An unchanged old body does not become newly illegal merely because a metadata edit now reaches the gate. A malformed envelope with multiple Reverse markers retains its existing refusal behavior.

requirements.heading: Ratchet algorithm
requirements.text: Pure address changes and generated Reverse-section refreshes do not run prose rules. A real authored-text or relevant metadata change does. BibTeX title edits check the resulting Literature title/envelope; Citation-key remapping alone follows the existing structural path.

requirements.heading: T-rule implementation

requirements.heading: Existing compiler shape

requirements.heading: Existing compiler shape
requirements.text: Use the existing argument parser, canonical JSON utilities, ledger, source manifests, operation prefixes, identified calls, and compact final-line convention. No PowerShell reimplementation of the compiler.

requirements.heading: Existing compiler shape
requirements.text: Keep a small fixed set of files under `the per-run term-cards`:

requirements.heading: Existing compiler shape
requirements.text: `plan.json` — Frozen rows, list/source fingerprints, jobs, limits, and compiler/rule version

requirements.heading: Existing compiler shape
requirements.text: `jobs/` — Per-job source-bound inputs

requirements.heading: Existing compiler shape
requirements.text: `out/` — Writer JSON, one stable output per writer job

requirements.heading: Existing compiler shape
requirements.text: `check/` and `review/` — Diagnostics and hash-bound review answers

requirements.heading: Existing compiler shape

requirements.heading: Existing compiler shape
requirements.text: The existing run ledger remains the scheduler. `state.json` is the compiler's recoverable artifact, not a second queue. Archive receipts are authoritative for committed writes.

requirements.heading: Plan inputs and grouping
requirements.text: Read the list by an explicit/unambiguous role, with a legacy table adapter for a pre-term book. Preserve its title/body fingerprints. Read source sections and the existing term-planning artifact when available.

requirements.heading: Plan inputs and grouping
requirements.text: For each row gather the exact name, avoid words, short meaning, first-definition locator, source file/line snippets, matching source sections, relevant notation, and neighboring terms.

requirements.heading: Plan inputs and grouping
requirements.text: Classify as math when the definition/snippet, applicable notation table, or known setting gives formal notation. A dollar sign is a useful candidate signal, not an infallible definition classifier. Record why it was classified. DeepSeek may promote a concept draft to math; promotion triggers the complete math checks and independent review before publication.

requirements.heading: Plan inputs and grouping
requirements.text: Group math terms one per job and concept terms four per job by default. Keep job ids stable by frozen row numbers. A grouped concept job that contains a promoted math draft can still finish, but its promoted term is not ready until its separate review passes.

requirements.heading: Writer, check, review, and one fix
requirements.text: Use the existing `Z.layer`/`Z.chain` and job `continue`/`fallback` fields. Do not implement the proposal sketch's `sameConversation` as a new orchestration option.

requirements.heading: Writer, check, review, and one fix
requirements.text: The chain is:

requirements.heading: Writer, check, review, and one fix
requirements.text: Readiness flow: write JSON; schema/render check; independent math review; one writer fix when needed; schema/render recheck; fresh review of changed math; publish readiness result.

requirements.heading: Writer, check, review, and one fix
requirements.text: A review names the term, source fingerprint, and exact draft/rendered-content hash. A previous `{"ok":true}` cannot approve a changed derivation. After the single fix, a fresh review may approve or refuse; a second refusal is final for that run. There is no unbounded review/fix loop.

requirements.heading: Writer, check, review, and one fix
requirements.text: A concept term needs schema/format checks but no mathematical reviewer. A changed schema or compiler renderer invalidates the corresponding readiness proof.

requirements.heading: Writer, check, review, and one fix
requirements.text: Do not ask a reviewer merely to endorse a formula. Its job includes all the proposal's depth requirements: domains/smoothness, definition fidelity, notation coverage, each transformation and basis, final claim, limits, numerical recomputation, skipped steps, and supplementation labels.

requirements.heading: DSMP management contract
requirements.text: Retain the existing managed path:

requirements.heading: DSMP management contract
requirements.text: Haiku managers, low effort, manage jobs and relay commands; they do not write Card prose or edit JSON on behalf of a writer.

requirements.heading: DSMP management contract
requirements.text: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash from the official source, high effort, writes/reviews/fixes content.

requirements.heading: DSMP management contract
requirements.text: At most eight conversations under one manager, and at most eight managers alive across the whole run.

requirements.heading: DSMP management contract
requirements.text: Writers, reviewers, and continuations share the global pool with the digest branch.

requirements.heading: DSMP management contract
requirements.text: Stable job ids and registered conversation/resource ids support cleanup and recovery.

requirements.heading: DSMP management contract
requirements.text: Collect answers promptly; retain a writer only through its permitted review/fix opportunity, then delete it. Review conversations are deleted after their answer is durably collected. Do not archive conversations.

requirements.heading: DSMP management contract
requirements.text: Remove the DeepSeek workspace registration once its work and required continuations are finished. Preserve the local staging/report files needed for audit; removing the workspace is not deletion of those files.

requirements.heading: DSMP management contract
requirements.text: Use the existing bounded retry/runtime budget. A provider failure gets the permitted single retry; a semantic content fix is a separate, finite step.

requirements.heading: DSMP management contract
requirements.text: The writer receives the applicable Chinese language skill through the existing job skills field, rather than copied skill text.

requirements.heading: DSMP management contract
requirements.text: Before parallelizing the two branches, verify the implementation holds global slots across a manager's actual lifetime, including review/fix continuations. Do not infer the total cap merely from `take:8` or the number of term jobs.

requirements.heading: DSMP management contract
requirements.text: Count retained writer conversations as live, even while idle. A manager cannot retain eight writers and then open eight reviewers. A simple schedule keeps the existing block of up to eight writer jobs but processes it in waves of at most four live writers, with at most four reviewer conversations alongside them. Review promoted terms from a grouped concept job sequentially within those slots. Complete the bounded fix/review opportunity and delete that wave before admitting the remaining writers. This needs no second pool, preserves the block/manager assignment, and avoids a global deadlock in which all 64 slots hold writers waiting for a reviewer slot.

requirements.heading: Publication, order, and recovery
requirements.text: For a new book, `terms -Step apply` creates the list as type `term` with no name. For a legacy book, the first publication includes a metadata-only retype; its authored body/title remain identical.

requirements.heading: Publication, order, and recovery
requirements.text: Publish the ready row prefix in order. For each row publish its head and complete continuation chain together when that chain fits a batch. Pack several small complete chains into a batch up to 64 operations and 1 MiB. A chain too large for one existing batch is refused for a bounded split/content fix; do not create a new large-batch API for it.

requirements.heading: Publication, order, and recovery
requirements.text: The first batch may also retype the list. Allocate Side children through `create_successor` and parts through Direct successors, using existing earlier-item references. Do not calculate an address and write it directly to SQLite.

requirements.heading: Publication, order, and recovery
requirements.text: Before publication verify the expected list and existing receipt-owned prefix. If unrelated Side children already occupy this structural slot, stop with a conflict rather than inserting/moving/deleting them to regain row order. The optional backfill plan must surface this condition before writing.

requirements.heading: Publication, order, and recovery
requirements.text: Example: rows 1–6 are ready, row 7 failed, rows 8–20 are ready. Publish 1–6; keep 8–20 staged. A repaired row 7 lets the next run publish 7–20 in order. Nothing is inserted before an existing head, and a failed row is never represented by a fake definition.

requirements.heading: Publication, order, and recovery
requirements.text: Use stable operation keys tied to run/unit/plan revision/step/row. On a transport interruption, query/replay the same request and receipts before replanning. Reuse verified returned addresses. Do not allocate a second head because the previous reply was lost.

requirements.heading: Publication, order, and recovery
requirements.text: A source/list/draft change creates a new plan revision. Reconcile already published receipt-owned Cards and report any conflict; never edit a historical accepted head merely because a new draft differs.

requirements.heading: Publication, order, and recovery
requirements.text: A book unit is `done` only when all its required rows and parts are verified. A partial prefix is useful committed work but leaves the book unit failed/blocked according to the existing ledger's states and its specific refusal. Do not mark a missing row done to release downstream dependencies.

requirements.heading: Compiler result
requirements.text: Report, per row:

requirements.heading: Compiler result
requirements.text: Source row number and exact term.

requirements.heading: Compiler result
requirements.text: Math/concept classification and whether promoted.

requirements.heading: Compiler result
requirements.text: Writer job, draft hash, check result, review hash/result, and fix disposition.

requirements.heading: Compiler result
requirements.text: Ready but not yet published, committed, refused, or conflicted status.

requirements.heading: Compiler result
requirements.text: Head/part addresses and receipt keys.

requirements.heading: Compiler result
requirements.text: Why publication stopped and which later ready drafts remain staged.

requirements.heading: Compiler result
requirements.text: For an incomplete stage the workflow continues to its read-only audit/report, but the feature is degraded. The ordinary dependency on a successful term-card book unit is not satisfied.

requirements.heading: Interface and scope
requirements.text: Command contract: zt-digest term-link -Step plan|apply -Staging <folder> [-CitationKey <key>] [-Occurrences first|all] [-Cards <addresses>] [-Token <claim>] [-Apply]

requirements.heading: Interface and scope
requirements.text: The default scope is the selected agent Literature tree. `-Cards` must be an exact subset of that tree. Reject other Workspaces, another book, Topic Cards, or ambiguous list selection.

requirements.heading: Interface and scope
requirements.text: Exclude the Literature root, the Term list, the book's structure/index/navigation Cards, and the Book notation table. Identify these through existing manifest/role information; do not skip any arbitrary Card merely because its title contains a common word.

requirements.heading: Interface and scope
requirements.text: Include term heads and parts, with their own term protected. Their use of other terms can link normally.

requirements.heading: Frozen plan
requirements.text: Read the tree once where practical, including raw bodies, metadata, list rows, current heads, and rule/policy information.

requirements.heading: Frozen plan
requirements.text: `term-link/plan.json` records:

requirements.heading: Frozen plan
requirements.text: Archive identity, book key, compiler/syntax version, and occurrence policy.

requirements.heading: Frozen plan
requirements.text: List, term-head mapping, and auto-link-choice fingerprints.

requirements.heading: Frozen plan
requirements.text: Input Card authored fingerprints and exact raw parsed body hashes.

requirements.heading: Frozen plan
requirements.text: Chosen substitutions and relevant skip reasons at UTF-8 byte offsets.

requirements.heading: Frozen plan
requirements.text: Output bodies or sufficient exact data to reproduce them.

requirements.heading: Frozen plan
requirements.text: Counts, unresolved target/label faults, and a stable plan content hash.

requirements.heading: Frozen plan
requirements.text: `preview.md` shows changed prose lines and totals. Reports can include timestamps, but the canonical transformation plan excludes clocks/run randomness so equal frozen inputs/options produce equal content. Sort Cards in natural address order and terms in row order.

requirements.heading: Normalization and preservation
requirements.text: Define `strip_term_links(B)` lexically, not by resolving targets: replace every syntactically valid Term-link macro outside protected literal syntax by its label.

requirements.heading: Normalization and preservation
requirements.text: For a book pass:

requirements.heading: Normalization and preservation
requirements.text: Retain foreign-book Term links as protected authored macros and report them. This proposal creates no cross-book uses.

requirements.heading: Normalization and preservation
requirements.text: Normalize same-book recognized Term macros to labels even if their old target is now missing or retyped. A stale target is precisely when address-resolution-based stripping would fail.

requirements.heading: Normalization and preservation
requirements.text: Refuse malformed Term-like markup for correction rather than guessing its intended label or deleting bytes.

requirements.heading: Normalization and preservation
requirements.text: Match and emit new same-book Term macros.

requirements.heading: Normalization and preservation
requirements.text: Verify `strip_term_links(new_body) == strip_term_links(old_body)` byte for byte.

requirements.heading: Normalization and preservation
requirements.text: This verification never strips ordinary Links. It does not normalize whitespace, punctuation, escapes, Unicode, math, or line endings. Use the parsed body returned by the archive as the baseline; do not claim preservation of pre-parser file formatting.

requirements.heading: Normalization and preservation
requirements.text: Title, metadata, and the Term list body are outside the pass and remain unchanged. Generated Reverse/Term-use sections may change because they are derived.

requirements.heading: Protected spans
requirements.text: Calculate source ranges without Markdown reserialization. Protect:

requirements.heading: Protected spans
requirements.text: Fenced and inline code — Literal examples must remain literal

requirements.heading: Protected spans
requirements.text: Inline/display math, including supported dollar and backslash forms — Terms inside formulas are not prose matches

requirements.heading: Protected spans
requirements.text: Ordinary Links and retained foreign Term links — Their macro bytes and targets must not change

requirements.heading: Protected spans
requirements.text: Markdown links/images, including reference-style forms — Do not change labels, destinations, or artifact/document syntax

requirements.heading: Protected spans
requirements.text: Raw HTML blocks/inline tags and chart fences — Never rewrite markup or executable chart content

requirements.heading: Protected spans
requirements.text: Heading lines and table rows — Navigation/labels and tables remain exact

requirements.heading: Protected spans
requirements.text: Source lines — Preserve citation/locator text

requirements.heading: Protected spans
requirements.text: Term head metadata lines — Preserve identity, category, avoid words, and auto-link policy

requirements.heading: Protected spans
requirements.text: The current term name anywhere in its own head/parts — No self-reference or redundant continuation use

requirements.heading: Protected spans
requirements.text: Generated Reverse text — It is not part of the authored body

requirements.heading: Protected spans
requirements.text: Use the shared scanner and existing Markdown offset facilities where appropriate. A syntax-aware offset walk can identify ranges; it must not render then parse the result back into source. If markup is incomplete and safe boundaries cannot be established, protect the uncertain tail or refuse the Card with a specific diagnostic. Never interpret an unclosed math/code span as permission to relink its contents.

requirements.heading: Protected spans
requirements.text: Only match within an individual eligible text range. Do not match across emphasis delimiters, escapes, an HTML tag, or any protected boundary. Conservative skipped matches are preferable to changing syntax.

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: There are at most 60 table terms by default. Start with a sorted literal candidate scan over link words and blockers. At each earliest match position choose the longest UTF-8-valid word, with stable row-order tie breaking. A blocker wins an exact tie with a link word.

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: This has a small fixed vocabulary and is easier to inspect than adding Aho–Corasick solely for this pass. Preserve leftmost-longest semantics. Switch algorithms only if the targeted benchmark shows a real need; an optimized matcher must pass the same fixtures.

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: Link words are exact term names with one valid head and auto-link enabled. Blockers include:

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: Every avoid word.

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: Every term name without a usable head or with auto-link disabled.

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: Nonlinkable short names.

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: Ambiguous unqualified forms of qualified homonyms.

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: For `学习（个体行为）` and `学习（产业生产率）`, the exact full forms can link, while the bare `学习` is a blocker. Do not mark the full qualified terms unusable merely because their bare form is ambiguous.

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: Use the proposal's conservative short-name default: do not link a one-Han-character term or a Latin name shorter than three letters. The stated acronym exception has no effect for `GDP` because it already has three letters; do not invent an exception for one-letter symbols.

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: Latin matches are case-sensitive and require ASCII word boundaries at both ends, treating letters, digits, and underscore as word characters. Han matches are literal, with the combined longest-match/blocker vocabulary reducing common substring mistakes. This is not semantic word segmentation; reports retain ambiguous/blocked cases for review.

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: Examples:

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: `净生产函数` and `生产函数` are terms — Link the longer full match

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: `替代弹性系数` is an avoid word — Consume it as a blocker; leave it unchanged

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: `相对要素价格` is nonlinkable but `要素价格` is linkable — Leave the longer full occurrence unchanged

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: `GDP` inside `GDPR` or `GDP_2024` — No match

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: A literal term split by Markdown emphasis — Skip; do not cross markup

requirements.heading: Simple matching is enough
requirements.text: With `first`, take the first eligible occurrence of each exact term per body. With `all`, take all eligible occurrences. Protected/blocked occurrences do not consume the first-occurrence allowance.

requirements.heading: Apply and concurrent changes
requirements.text: Apply revalidates archive identity, book/list/head mapping, policy contract, and each Card's authored guard. Recheck the preservation equation before sending each edit.

requirements.heading: Apply and concurrent changes
requirements.text: If the mapping/options/source list changed, invalidate the whole plan and build a new preview. If only one body changed before apply, explicitly replan that Card into a new plan revision and publish its updated preview/diff in the report. Do not silently edit from stale offsets.

requirements.heading: Apply and concurrent changes
requirements.text: Use `base_fingerprint` on every edit. A change after re-reading but before commit is a stale-base refusal, not a request to overwrite. Stop the affected chunk, retain committed receipts, and require bounded replanning. Never spin until another writer stops.

requirements.heading: Apply and concurrent changes
requirements.text: Pack unchanged-plan edits through existing identified-call chunks. A 300-Card book can require at least five calls even when every body fits the byte budget; more calls are possible for large bodies. There is at most one final edit per changed Card in a plan.

requirements.heading: Apply and concurrent changes
requirements.text: No-op Cards produce no edit. If the plan has no edits, write no receipt and advance no archive revision. Report no-op completion through the ledger's normal evidence path.

requirements.heading: Apply and concurrent changes
requirements.text: A `card_locked` response stops immediately with the typed tree/Lock facts and exit 2. A `card_check` response returns the fault lines for correction; relinking does not change visible prose to make the checker pass. With projection parity, retained style faults should remain legacy advice.

requirements.heading: Reports and guarantees
requirements.text: The report includes counts of scanned/changed Cards, added/retained/removed links, committed/pending chunks, missing heads, avoid words with Card/line, own-term skips, math/table/code skips, ambiguous bare forms, repeated occurrences, and foreign/malformed uses.

requirements.heading: Reports and guarantees
requirements.text: The guarantees are:

requirements.heading: Reports and guarantees
requirements.text: Deterministic transformation for equal frozen inputs.

requirements.heading: Reports and guarantees
requirements.text: Exact visible-body preservation by a checked equation.

requirements.heading: Reports and guarantees
requirements.text: Idempotence on an unchanged valid tree.

requirements.heading: Reports and guarantees
requirements.text: Bounded operations and recovery through receipts.

requirements.heading: Reports and guarantees
requirements.text: Access and Lock enforcement through the existing service.

requirements.heading: Reports and guarantees
requirements.text: No synonym correction, prose rewrite, term rename, or mathematical edit.

requirements.heading: Reports and guarantees
requirements.text: The matcher can miss a relationship or skip a potential use. It does not prove linguistic disambiguation. Count “Cards with no Term link” as an observation, not automatically a defect.

requirements.heading: Stage graph
requirements.text: Add base stages `term-cards` after `terms` and `term-link` after all Card writers and the term-card branch. Econ/math variants inherit the stages and retain their own writer order.

requirements.heading: Stage graph
requirements.text: Architecture/stage flow contract: ; terms --> digest["Digest and variant Card writers"]; terms --> tc["term-cards"]; digest --> bridge["Link, organize, figures, Bridge"]; bridge --> tl["term-link"]; tc --> tl; tl --> audit; audit --> finalize["Corrections -> scoped term-link -> final audit"]; finalize --> cleanup; cleanup --> report

requirements.heading: Stage graph
requirements.text: The `term-cards` branch uses frozen source sections and the shared term list. Concurrent model/digest writers do not own its Cards. New model notation is not an unstable live input: use the book's frozen notation/source; if a later cross-check finds a notation conflict, report it for a finite correction.

requirements.heading: Stage graph
requirements.text: The runtime can parallelize these branches through existing dependency edges. Do not add another worker pool. Verify that a slow term branch does not hold slots while waiting for writers it has no dependency on.

requirements.heading: Ledger units and truthful completion
requirements.text: `termcards/tNNN@1` — Term list prepared; job schema, shared check, required reviews/fix disposition verified

requirements.heading: Ledger units and truthful completion
requirements.text: `termcards/book@1` — Every required row ready and its expected head/parts committed and read back

requirements.heading: Ledger units and truthful completion
requirements.text: `termlink/book@1` — Successful term-card publication and every enabled Card-writer unit complete; plan applied/verified or proven no-op

requirements.heading: Ledger units and truthful completion
requirements.text: `termlink/final@R` — A finalization correction round R changed Cards; those Cards relinked and verified

requirements.heading: Ledger units and truthful completion
requirements.text: Use a generation/round identity for finalization rather than one reusable final unit that could suppress a later correction. This is an instance of the existing ledger plan-revision convention, not a new scheduling system.

requirements.heading: Ledger units and truthful completion
requirements.text: A failed term job can leave a published prefix and ready later drafts. The successful book dependency is still absent, so `term-link` is skipped/blocked with that reason in the normal full run. Audit/report must still run and show coverage debt. Do not mark failed job units done to force the pass.

requirements.heading: Ledger units and truthful completion
requirements.text: An explicit `term-link` mode may operate on the currently valid subset for diagnosis or backfill, reporting missing-head blockers. It does not mark the incomplete `termcards/book` done.

requirements.heading: Ledger units and truthful completion
requirements.text: If a layer is disabled by args, omit its ledger dependency rather than wait forever for an unregistered unit. Validate contradictory args early: requesting Term linking with no usable list/heads yields a clear skipped/incomplete result, not a successful zero-term book.

requirements.heading: Modes
requirements.text: `full` — Existing preparation and writers, term-card branch, term-link, audits/finalization

requirements.heading: Modes
requirements.text: `term-cards` — Validate existing book, source/sections preparation only, Term cards, Term links, audit, report

requirements.heading: Modes
requirements.text: `term-link` — Validate existing book and staging/manifest, deterministic pass, audit, report

requirements.heading: Modes
requirements.text: `resume` — Reconcile frozen plan, receipts, and registered units; resume only unfinished work

requirements.heading: Modes
requirements.text: Backfill preparation must create no new root, anchor, group, model, or narrative Card. Add a narrow sections-only branch to the existing prepare command if no such branch exists. It is not a second prepare pipeline.

requirements.heading: Modes
requirements.text: `term-link` mode needs no provider/source probe. `term-cards` needs source passages and the official provider path. Neither mode reruns ordinary digest/model stages.

requirements.heading: Modes
requirements.text: Declare the proposal's args in the base schema: `termCards`, `termLink`, `termCardsPerJob`, `termCardsMathPerJob`, `termLinkOccurrences`. Validate ranges/enums before dispatch. Limits can initially remain versioned tool defaults rather than adding more workflow knobs.

requirements.heading: Finalization and audits
requirements.text: The first Term-link pass runs after `bridge` and every enabled variant writer. For each finalization correction round, collect the actual changed Card addresses from its write results, then relink those Cards before the final read-only audit and math checks.

requirements.heading: Finalization and audits
requirements.text: If a correction changes a Term list, head name, or auto-link policy, its effect is book-wide: invalidate the mapping and run the whole-book Term-link plan. A changed-body-only correction can use `-Cards`.

requirements.heading: Finalization and audits
requirements.text: Do not add Term-link passes to every writer. The final write boundary is where deterministic linking belongs.

requirements.heading: Finalization and audits
requirements.text: Extend `audit` with the proposal's `terms` section: rows/heads/parts, math/concept, T faults, uses by Card type, no-use observations, remaining avoid words, and the ten most-used terms. Add generation/publication coverage and gate-contract metadata.

requirements.heading: Finalization and audits
requirements.text: Keep audit exit/completion distinct from book quality: “audit ran” does not mean “all terms passed.” Final reports contain `term_cards` and `term_link` with complete/degraded/skipped/refused status and counts.

requirements.heading: Writer compatibility
requirements.text: Add concise guidance to every relevant digest/card/fill/model/explain/correction prompt:

requirements.heading: Writer compatibility
requirements.text: Preserve existing Term macros, or write the visible term plainly.

requirements.heading: Writer compatibility
requirements.text: Do not manufacture target addresses or synonyms.

requirements.heading: Writer compatibility
requirements.text: Run the exact SELF-CHECK before submit.

requirements.heading: Writer compatibility
requirements.text: Treat `card_check` as content to fix through the current finite fix cycle.

requirements.heading: Writer compatibility
requirements.text: Treat `card_locked` as a planning stop, never a content retry.

requirements.heading: Writer compatibility
requirements.text: Deterministic compilers preflight through the shared core and, when placement/context is needed, service preview. Direct-writing workflows must also handle gate refusals. Ad-hoc agents remain protected by the gate even if they skip the optional tool.

requirements.heading: MCP changes
requirements.text: Preserve existing fields and add:

requirements.heading: MCP changes

stories.text: As a reader, I want one definition for Card legality, so that self-check and storage agree.
As a maintainer, I want one process-free rule core in the existing checker crate, so that reuse adds no gate service or dependency loop.
As a digest tool author, I want the existing run_lines interface and fixture ordering, so that current workflows retain behavior during extraction.
As a Card author, I want structured actionable diagnostics, so that I can fix the exact rejected requirement.
As an owner, I want retained legacy faults to remain advisory, so that old Cards stay editable.
As an owner, I want new duplicate faults to be distinguished from retained faults, so that edits cannot quietly worsen quality.
As an author, I want new type and formal-role rules applied on metadata changes, so that retyping cannot bypass format checks.
As an owner, I want archive- and Workspace-specific policy, so that human notes and agent digest standards can differ.
As an owner, I want validated policy set/reset and visible defaults, so that configuration typos cannot weaken unrelated checks.
As an author, I want policy advice and hard invariants distinguished, so that warnings do not grant Access or unlock a tree.
As a maintainer, I want graph-only rules kept in audits, so that writes do not scan the whole box.

criteria.text: The existing checker crate builds as a pure library with default features disabled; its core cannot read files, start MCP, launch processes, or import process-platform dependencies.
The standalone executable and digest library caller keep their existing entry points and ordered fixture output during the extraction; existing CLI input modes still work.

One pure text implementation owns envelope parsing, repeated-title checks, term-table compatibility parsing, and lexical Link operations; the root retains its existing address grammar and lifecycle facade.
The root service links this core without a dependency cycle; the normal checker/digest builds retain the optional CLI/MCP adapter.
Move rule code before changing policy semantics, preserve compatibility re-exports, and demonstrate parity against existing fixtures rather than tests that merely mirror new internals.
Update the checker and affected Cards/service wiki descriptions with the code, including the changed service-redeploy implication of shared rules.
Each diagnostic carries address, rule, fault code, unclipped semantic identity, full message, severity, legacy flag, and scope; human lines preserve current formatting and order.
Compare old and proposed versions under the same current policy/rule snapshot, consuming a multiset of comparable fault identities rather than a set of clipped lines.
Moving unchanged faulty prose retains legacy advice; duplicating the same faulty sentence introduces a new occurrence; different messages sharing a clipped prefix stay distinct.
Size-fault identity includes measured value and limit, missing-label identity includes the missing set, and fragment faults include full offending text.
Retypes, role changes, and concept-to-formal transitions grandfather only unchanged applicability signatures; newly relevant requirements must be met.
New Cards have no legacy allowance; hard envelope/field/Access/Lock/Link invariants retain their existing mandatory behavior and specific legacy exceptions.
No persistent baseline table is added; old/new evaluation against a changed rule version is explicit and covered by fixtures.
An unchanged legacy repeated leading title retains the existing authored-changed allowance, while multiple Reverse markers retain their existing refusal.

Persist declared gate.<workspace>.<rule> overrides in the existing archive metadata; default/reset semantics, effective policy output, archive identity, policy hash, and revision change are observable.
Support only block, advise, and off for valid configurable rules; reject unknown Workspaces/rules/values and attempts to disable mandatory field/Link/Access/Lock invariants.
Honor every human/agent default and advisory subcase in the attached requirements, including R6 human off/agent advise, concept-model exemptions, T4 advice, and T8/graph audit-only behavior.
Reject graph-only blocking overrides rather than running whole-Workspace graph work during a write.
One operation or atomic batch uses a single effective policy snapshot; changing an override in one archive/Workspace does not change another.
R22/T10 and envelope/R19 have one diagnostic owner and do not double-count the same fault; only mechanically implemented rules are enforced.
Policy rollout can advise newly added quality rules while preserving current mandatory checks; activation rewrites no Cards and saves no legacy baseline.
Resolve the final candidate address/kind/Workspace/text/type/facet/level/form/term name before evaluation, and read required context from the same write transaction.
Enforce Access and Locks before authored changes, gather bounded parent/book/setting/target context, and never build the whole archive snapshot for each Card.
Cover root/successor/insert creates, edits, retypes, relevant metadata-only changes, Literature titles, direct shell/Session setters, GUI writes, MCP writes, and batch item writers.
A blocking result leaves no Card/id/allocation/receipt/revision residue; an accepted result retains existing fields and carries operation-owned structured warnings with version/hash.
Typed card_check includes address, blocker count, ordered fault lines and diagnostics; batch callers can add index/tool/op-key identity without parsing the human string.
GUI and Session retain the draft/edit buffer after refusal; successful advice is shown compactly through existing result surfaces, without a new approval dialog.
Distinguish absent semantic context from failed/unavailable context, and refuse an incomplete write check rather than silently passing or truncating large context.
Pure structural moves/key remapping and generated Reverse refreshes keep their existing rules rather than invoking prose checks; import/restore authoring routes are explicitly classified.
There is no global warning buffer, no second writer mutex, no gate process, no new Card database, and no Access/Lock bypass through policy.
Keep real batches limited to 1–64 items and 1 MiB; one blocking item rolls back every item, receipt, allocation, and revision of that batch.
Later items see earlier successful transaction candidates; Term targets created earlier can resolve, and forward references remain unsupported.
Preview uses the same writer/gate path, collects typed card_check and Lock refusals independently, and marks dependent unbound-reference items blocked rather than fabricating context.
Preview returns complete/checked/refused/blocked counts, diagnostics, warnings, projected Cards, and archive revision; it persists no Card/receipt/allocation/Lock history.
Retain existing 1,024-item/8-MiB preview-sequence bounds; a large preview does not raise the real write cap or reserve future successful chunks.
Real refusals identify the failing zero-based item/tool/op-key while preserving the existing human item-number convention.
Lost responses and replays retain current durable receipt semantics; committed earlier chunks of a larger operation remain distinguishable from the refused chunk.
Retain --json, --model, --addresses, --cards, and run_lines; add --draft, draft --workspace default agent, and structured complete/contract output.
Draft bundles accept exact candidate text/type/term metadata, optional prior state, explicit context completeness, and optional version/policy binding; unknown placement remains incomplete.
Stored live Cards use their actual Workspace and reject a conflicting override; offline built-in policy is explicitly identified when archive policy is unavailable.

Publish authoritative running-service rule version, diagnostic schema, effective policy/hash, limits/applicability, archive id/revision, and term capabilities through existing verified reads/writes; expose zt_check_version at initialization too.
Detect proxy/daemon or CLI/service version drift; a mismatch or missing required context never exits as a successful acceptance prediction.
At the coordinated compatibility switch, every mode counts blockers only in faults:N, tags advice consistently, and migrates digest callers that count lines or maintain private advisory lists.
CLI exits 0 for complete/no blockers, 1 for complete/blockers, and 2 for invalid/incomplete/stale/infrastructure outcomes; a self-check reserves no future write.
Reuse service preview for placement-dependent preflight; add no check_cards tool or extra policy endpoint and preserve the Literature scope/box pin in the client.
Add type term and one nullable term_name column; root Cards remain Idea Cards, unrelated model/hub/math fields are invalid, and non-Term Cards cannot hold a term name.
Omitted term preserves its value, null or trimmed-empty clears it, and a supplied name is one line of at most 40 Unicode scalar values with no brackets, @, pipe, or backtick.
Retyping away from term clears the field; explicit incompatible field input is rejected; create/insert/edit/batch fields and basic type filters expose the value.
Consistently back up and transactionally rebuild the Card CHECK to include term, preserve every old row id/text/identity/type field, and recreate current indexes/protection.
Extend authored/SQL frozen-field fingerprints for nonempty names without changing hashes of existing null-name Cards; update every explicit column list and wrapper caller.
Keep Lock hashing distinct from canonical receipt hashing, and synchronize the service/digest receipt projection for nonempty term names.
Validate generation-1 protection/evidence, install term-aware generation 2 through a guarded upgrade, preserve historical events/seals/pins, and distinguish legitimate old triggers from tampering.
Prove the baseline binary refuses generation 2 before mutation; a policy rollback is not schema compatibility and unsupported ancient clients remain outside the release contract.
Changing only a name on a Locked member is refused; an unlocked pinned target keeps existing editable-field semantics and may produce label-mismatch advice.
Compute list/card/part/unfiled roles from type, optional name, immediate Side placement, and same-name Direct continuation; never persist a role or ownership table.
Expose name, wire role card for heads, owning list, use count, rows/parts/uses/faults and consistent archive revision in existing reads/new get_terms.
Report all seven named structure faults: unfiled, duplicate, row-without-card, card-without-row, part-name, label-mismatch, and invalid target.
Get_terms accepts a list or unambiguous descendant; ambiguous book/list selection, unsupported read bounds, and cycles/depth limits fail visibly rather than silently selecting or truncating.
Preserve existing R6 table parsing and avoid-word splitting, while detecting raw exact/case-equivalent duplicate rows before compatibility deduplication for publication.
Keep exact table-row spelling with no transliteration, normalization, synonym rewrite, qualifier stripping, or case folding during linking.
Structure/coverage faults remain reportable during partial construction; a valid head does not require all other rows to be published.
Render exact term titles, ordered head labels/common sections/source locators and applicable original wording, distinctions, misreadings, book role and plain explanation.

Math terms contain explicit hypotheses/domains, tagged definition/reading, notation/ranges, reasoned equivalent forms, numbered justified steps/results, limits, computed examples, intuition, and source-fidelity supplement labels.
Persist disabled automatic linking and its required reason as recognized authored metadata lines; absence means enabled and the list table gains no column/comment.

Partition whole derivation/content blocks deterministically into same-name Direct parts with continuation titles and explicit head/notation references; do not repeat head-only requirements on every part.
Enforce 12 steps and 1,600 measured prose units per Card, excluding formulas/tables; refuse an unsplittable oversized block or oversized mandatory head rather than truncate or silently raise limits.
Implement every applicable T1–T10 predicate with head/part/chain distinctions, applying T9 in place of Idea-size rules; T4 stays advisory and T10 shares R22 without duplicate faults.
Concept terms reject formal derivation sections while allowing legitimate inline formulas; approximate symbol/phrase checks cannot claim mathematical proof.
Reject unknown/misordered sections and identity/row mismatches, preserve existing sentence-language rules, and compare manual/draft outputs through the same evaluator.
Every proposal JSON field and source-fidelity requirement is either rendered, used for deterministic publication/link policy, or explicitly validated; no required content is silently discarded.

Validate and retain the full draft content contract: term/original/category/link/link_reason/first_defined; explanation sentences; book_definition text/section/quote; hypothesis id/text; definition formula/reading; symbols symbol/meaning/type/auxiliary; equivalent formula/reason; derivation claim/steps(text,basis,formula)/result; limits case/text/formula; example/intuition/distinctions(term,text)/misreadings/role_in_book.

Writer jobs request 3–8 explanation sentences, 1–4 book-definition and book-role sentences, 2–5 intuition sentences for mathematics, explicit auxiliary symbols and exact neighboring names; a concept term need not invent mathematical material.
T6 covers 易知, 显然, 不难看出, 容易证明 and 同理可得 without an expanded/named step; named earlier-step 同理 references remain allowed.
Parse [[label@address]] using the first @, enforce the shared 1–40-scalar label grammar and Regular Location grammar, and preserve strict/tolerant behavior.
Expose whole macro, target-only, and optional label byte ranges into the original UTF-8 input; rewrite operations alter only target bytes.
A new Term occurrence must target an existing computed head rather than list/part/other type; retained invalid uses follow the specified multiplicity-aware legacy exception.
Labels differing from target names are reported without silently changing words; malformed or changed-invalid targets are not grandfathered as retained uses.
Term-like examples inside literal inline/fenced code and inline/display math are not uses; preserve ordinary Link interpretation while using broader protection only for the relinker.
All scanner consumers reuse the same lexical implementation; no digest/checker/scope regex independently interprets label@target.
Raw Card bodies and exports retain macros and existing ordinary Citation-key/Location Link behavior is unchanged.
Store term as the syntax-assigned occurrence kind in the existing index and derive labels from authoritative source/ordinal parsing, without a second label table/column.
Generate separate ordinary Reverse links and Term uses under the existing generated marker, omit empty sections, and deduplicate sources independently in each section.
A source containing both an ordinary Link and a Term use appears once in each relevant section; generated text is never reindexed as authored Links.
Moves/compaction/key rename rewrite only addresses, preserve labels, include Term occurrences in all mutation plans, and respect human-body rewrite refusal for agents.
Term links create distinct cross-tree Lock pins like ordinary authored Links; same-tree uses create no external pin and Locked sources refuse relinking edits.
Broken/non-head targets carry source/target/label facts in CLI/MCP/GUI reports; retyping a head does not falsely make an invalid Term use valid.
Indexed and full-lifecycle outputs agree on occurrence order, ordinary Reverse sections, Term uses, and broken targets across interruption and rebuild fixtures.
Use one syntax-aware label projection before existing ordinary-Link stripping, so R2/R4/R6/R7/R9 and size checks read the actual visible sentence.
A Term link to a Topic Card is still refused by the digest Literature scope using the target after @, and scope does not become a general Access rule.
Get_card/get_cards/get_tree raw reads remain the default; optional term_links:label returns marked projected text through the shared helper.
Projected bodies never become edit bases, receipt hashes, or authored fingerprints; stages that edit retain/fetch guarded raw text.
Read-only digest/group/Bridge/idea-grow prompt consumers can use projection without losing words or authoring Term macros themselves.
Statement comparison ignores only Term markup in addition to its established limited normalization; formulas, values, signs, variables, negation, assumptions, and scope remain significant.
Adding or moving only Term markup cannot invent a new visible-language fault, while changing a visible label remains a real prose change.
Render only the label in the prose font with a restrained dotted underline; ordinary reasoned Links retain their address/title chip.
Hover and keyboard focus expose the short list-row meaning/address; click and keyboard activation use existing encoded Card navigation.
Broken links show an accessible broken explanation and cross-Workspace styling retains current meaning; the UI does not depend on hover alone.
Escape labels/meanings/targets/attributes separately from URL encoding and prove malicious text cannot become HTML or route injection.
Use the existing Term Card reader, quiet metadata, ordinary Markdown sections, and a collapsed generated-use count/disclosure.
Preserve exact list rendering/body and successor navigation; no new board, popover service, or parallel Card page is added.
The existing Regular-Card type picker and term-name input support create/edit/retype/null-clear semantics and suppress incompatible fields.
Completion searches heads by name and disambiguates book/address; choosing a Term use inserts the exact labeled macro without inventing an address.
Ordinary reasoned citation to the same Term Card remains available, distinct from inserting a Term use.
Create/insert/edit/batch enums, server instructions, CLI type/name arguments, tree counts, type filters, search chips, and category classifiers recognize the sixth type.

Existing idea-grow/R6 consumers still parse the unchanged list body; default relevance ranking is not silently expanded into the register tier.

Column advance, wrapping, mouse hit testing, and link-follow selection use display width rather than macro bytes.
Han wide characters and combining marks have correct ranges and copying/selection offsets; hidden addresses cannot shift the visible text.
Raw edit mode retains complete macros and ordinary Link rendering/following remains unchanged.
Type/help and warning/refusal presentation integrate with existing Session conventions and retain the edit buffer.
Term kind is assigned by syntax and never inferred from prose; it cannot become an inherited ordinary relation kind.
Preserve prior relevant ordinary relation inheritance across a Term occurrence and ensure a following ordinary Link never inherits term.
Term occurrences do not affect Idea inbound/outbound credit, reason rules L1–L3, Model membership/relations/neighbors, or Model-board placement.
General Link/broken/Lock consumers continue seeing every Term occurrence; filtering reasoning does not hide integrity facts.

Dumps include the existing type map and nullable/omitted term-name manifest convention, retaining raw macros and all heads/parts.
Round-trip authored identity, addresses, row-sensitive Lock facts, use sections, and ordinary Link data without losing term fields.
Markdown export never substitutes projected labels for raw authored macros; projected reads stay opt-in and marked.
Capability/schema floor prevents supported older binaries from writing the new archive or silently dropping fields; baseline generation-2 startup refusal is verified.

Expose all declared term-cards command steps/options and compact final-line conventions through existing argument parsing/command dispatch.
Freeze list/source fingerprints, exact rows, source file/line definition snippets, occurrence sections, notation, neighboring names/meanings, limits, and checker/compiler versions.
Classify math/concept with recorded evidence and allow a later concept-to-math promotion to require full mathematical readiness.

Reuse existing plan/jobs/out/check/review/state/report artifacts and ledger/resource machinery; no second queue, provider broker, or terminology database.

Every math term, including a promoted concept draft, is reviewed in a fresh conversation for hypotheses, source definition, notation, every step/basis/result, limits and recomputed example.

Send one finite fix prompt to the original writer through existing continue/fallback job fields; changed math drafts require an independent re-review.
A second refusal after the permitted fix is final for that run; concept terms need no mathematical reviewer and there is no unbounded correction loop.
Retain source-fidelity supplementation labels and report actual executed numerical checks without claiming unperformed verification or formal proof.
Report readiness separately from publication, with structured per-term faults and hashes; apply still rechecks through the service.
Haiku low-effort managers relay/manage only; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash official/high-effort jobs write/review/fix JSON and receive skills via the job field.
Keep at most eight live managers globally and eight live conversations per manager, including idle retained writers and review/fix continuations.

Bind runtime policy to the current managed protocol, preserving the proposal budget of at most 240 minutes per conversation and bounded polling (nonblocking polls of all open sessions and at most 90 seconds blocking on one); one permitted provider retry is distinct from the one semantic fix. Reconcile an actual protocol change explicitly rather than silently increasing these limits.
New list publication uses type term from the start; legacy lists are metadata-only retyped with exact authored title/body/Links/address/row identity preserved.

Do not match across emphasis/escapes/tags/protected boundaries; protect or refuse uncertain incomplete syntax tails.
Use a simple sorted literal leftmost-longest scan over at most the default 60 terms and avoid/nonlinkable/ambiguous blockers, with blocker precedence on ties.
Honor exact spelling, full qualified homonyms, conservative short names and case-sensitive ASCII word boundaries; avoid words remain unchanged and unlinked.
First means the first eligible unblocked occurrence per term/body, all means every eligible occurrence; protected matches do not consume first.
